questions.question: How do you perform CRUD operations in ActiveRecord with examples?
questions.title: ActiveRecord CRUD Operations
questions.direct_answer: The CRUD operations in ActiveRecord: create with User.create(name: 'Ada') (builds, saves, returns the record) or u = User.new(...); u.save; read with User.find(1), User.where(role: 'admin'), User.all; update with u.update(name: 'Bob') (validates and saves) or u.name = 'Bob'; u.save; delete with u.destroy (runs callbacks) or u.delete (skips them). Each operation returns the record or a relation and runs the SQL for you, with validations on save/update and callbacks on destroy.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you can write each CRUD operation concretely and note validations (on save/update) and callbacks (on destroy).
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Using delete (skips callbacks) or not handling failed validations (save/update return false).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: create (build+save), find/where (read), update (set+save+validate), destroy (delete+callbacks). Check the return — save/update can fail validations.

sections.title: What the interviewer wants
sections.content: Define ActiveRecord CRUD Operations simply, show a small example, and mention the main trade-off or edge case.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: create builds, validates, and saves in one step; new + save does it in two.
find(id) raises if missing; find_by returns nil; where returns a relation.
update sets, validates, and saves; save/update return false on validation failure — check it.
destroy runs callbacks then deletes; delete skips callbacks — avoid unless you mean it.
Validations run on create/save/update; callbacks run on save and destroy (not on delete).

sections.title: Spoken Answer
sections.content: The CRUD operations in ActiveRecord, concretely. Create is User.create of name and email, which builds, saves, and returns the record, or User.new then save, where save returns true or false depending on validations. Read is find of 1, which raises if missing, where of role admin, which returns a relation, or all. Update is update of name, which sets attributes, runs validations, and saves, or you set the attribute and call save. Delete is destroy, which runs callbacks then deletes the row, or delete, which skips callbacks. Each runs the SQL for you. A common mistake is using delete instead of destroy, because delete skips callbacks like auditing, and not checking save and update's return, because they return false if validations fail, which is silent data loss. Use find when you want to raise on missing, and find_by when you want nil.

sections.title: Build the mental model
sections.content:
The CRUD operations in ActiveRecord: create with User.create(name: 'Ada') (builds, saves, returns the record) or u = User.new(...); u.save; read with User.find(1), User.where(role: 'admin'), User.all; update with u.update(name: 'Bob') (validates and saves) or u.name = 'Bob'; u.save; delete with u.destroy (runs callbacks) or u.delete (skips them).

Each operation returns the record or a relation and runs the SQL for you, with validations on save/update and callbacks on destroy.

A common mistake is using delete (skips callbacks) or not handling failed validations (save/update return false).

sections.title: The CRUD Flow
sections.content:
Create -> Read -> Update -> Delete, with validations and callbacks at the right steps.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  C[create / new+save] -->|validates| R[find/where/all]
  R --> U[update: validates+saves]
  U --> D[destroy: callbacks then delete]
```

sections.title: CRUD operations in detail
sections.content:
```ruby
# CREATE: build + save
user = User.create(name: 'Ada', email: 'ada@x.com')  # saves, returns record
#   or step by step:
u = User.new(name: 'Ada'); u.save   # save returns true/false (validations!)

# READ
User.find(1)                  # by id (raises RecordNotFound if missing)
User.where(role: 'admin')     # relation (lazy)
User.all                      # all rows

# UPDATE: set + validate + save
user.update(name: 'Bob')      # returns true/false; saves if valid
#   or: user.name = 'Bob'; user.save

# DELETE
user.destroy                 # runs callbacks, then deletes the row
user.delete                  # deletes WITHOUT callbacks (avoid unless you mean it)
```
